Zhmerynka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Zhmerynka grew around a railway station established in 1865, with the first train arriving in 1870. During Romanian administration in WWII, its ghetto could not prevent the execution of 286 Jews brought here from Brailiv, documented elsewhere in this collection, though many local Jews survived — almost 1,000 remained in the ghetto by June 1944. In December 1944, in a remarkable act of open defiance under emerging Soviet rule, young Zhmerynka Jews organized a clandestine Zionist group and sent a letter directly to the Communist Party newspaper Pravda requesting permission to emigrate to Israel. This cemetery, established in 1884, sits adjacent to the town's Christian cemetery and remains in use today, with about 3,000 surviving gravestones.
